text.content: Checkpoint 1: Thinking about cross-references

rich_text.plain_text: Checkpoint 1: Thinking about cross-references

text.content: - The SME Loan Product Guide references the same eligibility threshold in three different sections. If a fixed text splitter cuts across those sections without overlap, each chunk contains only one piece of the picture. When a client asks a question that requires all three in context, the agent retrieves whichever chunk scored highest in similarity. The client receives a partial answer that appears complete.

text.content: Checkpoint 2: Thinking about chunk overlap

rich_text.plain_text: Checkpoint 2: Thinking about chunk overlap

text.content: - Overlap adds a defined number of tokens shared between consecutive chunks, reducing the risk of splitting a meaningful unit at the boundary. For a dense legal or financial document, a small overlap may still cut mid-clause, while a large overlap stores significant amounts of redundant content across many chunks. The right overlap value is the smallest number that keeps critical clause boundaries intact.

text.content: Checkpoint 3: Thinking about tabular data

rich_text.plain_text: Checkpoint 3: Thinking about tabular data

text.content: - A text splitter reads a table sequentially and loses the column relationships that give the data its meaning. A chunk produced from a five-column rate table might read "SME Standard 5.2% SME Plus 4.8% SME Flex 5.5%" with no headers to indicate what those figures represent. When a client asks about the SME Plus interest rate, the agent retrieves that chunk and has no reliable way to isolate the correct figure from the string of concatenated values.

text.content: Checkpoint 4: Thinking about metadata

rich_text.plain_text: Checkpoint 4: Thinking about metadata

text.content: - Every chunk stored in the vector database carries metadata alongside its vector. Semantic similarity search finds chunks that are mathematically close to the query, but two chunks from different sections of the product guide might score similarly for the same query. A "section" metadata field gives the retrieval system an additional filter: if the query is about eligibility criteria, chunks tagged with the eligibility section can be prioritised over chunks from the rate structure section that happened to score similarly.

text.content: Takeaway:

rich_text.plain_text: Takeaway:

text.content: Document preparation is a design decision that determines how much of the document's meaning survives the ingestion process. A chunk boundary in the wrong place destroys context. A table processed as sequential text loses its structure entirely. The investment in preparing documents correctly before ingestion pays back every time the agent retrieves accurately.
